thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert triggered for tenant=bandit (dedicated-reserved). Alert: reserved_pool_io_latency_p99 > 2500ms for 5m, errors(5xx) spike 12%
PagerDuty: https://pagerduty.com/incidents/PD-85342 (severity: high)

Sam: acked. I'm on-call. any immediate customer-facing impact?

Maya: confirmed latency and 5xxs from metrics (grafana link). p95 ~ 1.2s, p99 ~ 2.7s, error-rate ~12% over last 8m. KV cache evictions spiked right before.

Kevin: seeing lots of KV eviction logs on the cluster: `kvcache: evict 0x9f3a...` repeated. Likely memory pressure on reserved nodes -> fallback to cold path increasing latency.

Rachel: @Sam @Kevin do we have burst capacity left for bandit this window?

Maya: their reserved pool = 4 GPUs, burst pool configured = 2, current burst usage = 100%. No autoscale headroom.

Sam: okay immediate plan: 1) soft-rate limit bandit to reduce incoming QPS 2) try a rolling restart of kvcache service on one host to free mem 3) if that fails, expand reserved pool by +1 GPU and move some traffic.

Kevin: doing soft-limit now. Running rate limiter rule:```bash
rwctl routing rate-limit add --tenant bandit --qps 250 --reason "temp mitigation"
```

Kevin: applied. Monitor for ~30s.

Maya: restarting kvcache on node gpu-42 now (rolling, not all at once). Logs:```
[2026-03-15T08:12:03Z] kvcache: shutdown triggered
[2026-03-15T08:12:10Z] kvcache: warmup complete, entries restored: 87%
```

Maya: p99 down to 1.9s, errors -> 7%

Sam: good. but still above target. I'm going to try expanding reserved pool. Kevin, can you prepare the scale command and run if ops approves?

Kevin: prepared:```bash
rwctl reserved scale --tenant bandit --delta-gpus 1 --mode immediate
```

OpsBot: Note: scaling consumes reserved quota; will bill per-commit pricing. Approve with `/ops approve scale bandit +1`

Sam: /ops approve scale bandit +1 (approved) :white_check_mark:

Kevin: running scale...

incident-bot: scaling job started: scale-job-9982 (tracking)

PagerDuty: escalation: paging L2 oncall (Rachel) due to ongoing errors

Rachel: I'm on it, joining bridge. creating incident bridge: https://zoom.us/j/123-456-789

Maya: scale completed on infra side. new node joined, kvcache rebuilt. p99 back to 750ms, error-rate ~1.8% after warmup ~3m.

Sam: excellent. customer impact window estimate: ~12 minutes of degraded responses, peak error-rate ~12%, affecting production traffic for tenant bandit. Noted that requests to fallback model variant spiked during eviction.

Rachel: I'll own post-incident follow-up and blameless postmortem. Items: KV cache memory tuning, reserved burst headroom alerting, add auto-expand runbook for enterprise tenants.

Kevin: logging the commands and timestamps into the incident ticket: PD-85342. Also adding the temporary rate-limit rule id=rl-774 to the ticket.

Sam: handoff: I'm going offline in 10m. @Rachel take primary for ongoing mitigation and follow-up.

Rachel: taking over. updating customer success: @account-team-bandit (email) and sending status update: "We observed elevated latency and errors; mitigated by adding +1 GPU to reserved pool and temporary QPS limits. Full postmortem to follow." :email:

Maya: note for postmortem: Prometheus query used -> `sum(rate(kv_eviction_total[5m])) by (node)` and `histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))`

Rachel: thanks. I'll create the incident doc in /docs/incidents/bandit-2026-03-15 and assign action owners.

Sam: thumbs up. closing on-call thread but leaving PD open until postmortem created. Thanks team :raised_hands:

incident-bot: PagerDuty incident PD-85342: status=acknowledged, assignee=Rachel, severity=high

Rachel: marking this thread as handed off at 3333338200 and will update once postmortem draft exists.

Kevin: leaving a note: potential follow-up tuning: bump kvcache default reserve to 30% for enterprise tenants, add early eviction alert at 5 evictions/min.

Maya: adding dashboard panel for reserved-burst-usage and kvcache-evictions for bandit (done).

Rachel: closing thread here. If anything regresses ping me directly. :point_up:
